A model in dMod2 is a chain of function objects, each returning an output together with the
derivatives with respect to the parameters:

| class | constructors | mapping |
|---|---|---|
| `parfn` | `P()`, `Pexpl()`, `Pimpl()` | outer to inner parameters per condition, or parameters to a steady state (`Pimpl()`) |
| `prdfn` | `Xs()`, `Xf()` | parameters to state trajectories, with sensitivities (`Xs()`) or without (`Xf()`) |
| `obsfn` | `Y()` | states to observables, observables to standard deviations (error model) |
| `objfn` | `normL2()`, `constraintL2()`, `datapointL2()`, `constraintStability()` | parameters to $-2 \log L$ with gradient and Hessian |

`*` concatenates two objects by the chain rule. For $y = g(x(p(\theta)))$,

$$\frac{\partial y}{\partial \theta} = \frac{\partial g}{\partial x}\,\frac{\partial x}{\partial p}\,
\frac{\partial p}{\partial \theta},$$

each factor computed exactly by the object it belongs to, the middle one from the sensitivity equations.
`g*x*pSS*p` maps the outer parameters to the observables of all conditions,
`normL2(data, g*x*pSS*p, e)` is the objective, and `+` adds objectives, e.g. a prior. Inner
parameters are the symbols of the equations, with values per condition; outer parameters are
those of the fit, shared by all conditions they enter.

The guide uses the model of Oppelt et al. [@oppelt2018model], NFκB signaling in HepG2 cells after
TNFα, from the project
[`examples/oppeltNPJSystBiolAppl2018`](https://github.com/dModverse/dMod2/tree/master/examples/oppeltNPJSystBiolAppl2018).
This chapter follows `model.R`, the full model of the publication.

```{r setup}
```

## Reaction network

TNFα activates the receptor, the receptor activates IKK, and IKK phosphorylates IκBα and NFκB in
their complex. Phosphorylated IκBα is degraded, free NFκB enters the nucleus and induces IκBα and
A20. IκBα exports NFκB, A20 inhibits IKK activation; the two negative feedbacks give damped
oscillations of nuclear NFκB. IKK passes through the states `Ikk`, `pIkk`, `ppIkk` and the
refractory `iIkk`.

`addReaction()` adds a reaction to an `eqnlist`. `assignCompartment()` places the four nuclear
species in the nucleus of volume `Vnuc` relative to the cytoplasm. Rates are concentration rates
in the compartment of the educts, of the products for a reaction without net educts, so

$$\dot x_i = \frac{1}{V_i} \sum_r S_{ri}\, V_{c(r)}\, v_r(x, p),$$

with $S_{ri}$ the stoichiometry and $V_{c(r)}$ the volume of the compartment of reaction $r$.
TNFα is not used up: the reaction `TNF -> TNF + TNFR` keeps it constant as a catalyst.

```{r reactions, echo = FALSE}
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
# one row per reaction, both sides as written in addReaction(), so that a catalyst appears on
# both sides; the chunk runs again with an addReaction() that records the arguments
written <- list()
record <- new.env()
record$addReaction <- function(eqnlist, from, to, rate, description = names(rate), ...) {
  force(eqnlist)
  written[[length(written) + 1L]] <<- data.frame(from = from, to = to, rate = unname(rate),
                                                 description = description)
  dMod2::addReaction(eqnlist, from, to, rate, description, ...)
}
eval(parse(text = knitr::knit_code$get("reactions")), record)
written <- do.call(rbind, written)
stopifnot(identical(written$rate, unname(as.character(reactions$rates))))
side <- function(v) ifelse(v == "", "∅", sprintf("`%s`", v))
knitr::kable(data.frame(reaction = paste(side(written$from), "→", side(written$to)),
                        rate = sprintf("`%s`", written$rate), description = written$description),
             row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r, ref.label = "reactions", eval = FALSE}
```

Expressions follow the
[expression language of cppDE](https://dmodverse.github.io/cppDE/reference/expressions.html).
Factors named `eta_` relate two rates, e.g. `eta_form_complex_nuc` the nuclear to the cytoplasmic
complex formation.

```{r}
length(reactions$states)
as.eqnvec(reactions)[c("NfkIkb", "nNfk", "TNF", "TNFR")]
```

## Observation functions

The data are live-cell imaging of NFκB and A20-GFP, immunoblots of the cytoplasm, and immunoblots
after immunoprecipitation of NFκB or IκBα. Each readout but the ratio `ratioNFkBIkBa` measures a
sum of species up to a scale `s_` and an offset `off_`; imaging signals bleach with rate `tau_`. On the natural log scale of
the data,

$$y = \log(s\, x + o) - \tau t .$$

```{r observables}
```

## Error model

Blots have a standard deviation per point in the column `sigma`. The imaging readouts get an
estimated standard deviation on the log scale; rows with a value in `sigma` ignore the error model.

```{r errors}
```

## Steady-state constraints

The cells rest before TNFα. NFκB and IKK are conserved, so $f(x, p) = 0$ determines the resting
state only together with the totals:

```{r}
conservedQuantities(reactions)
```

`Pimpl()` solves the steady state numerically in every evaluation, with the totals `totalNfk` and
`totalIkk` as parameters, `TNF` held at 0, and exact derivatives of the root
([Methods > Steady states](methods-steady-states.html)). `steadyStates()`, the analytic
alternative, solves the balances of this network for the rate constants `eta_int_Ikb` and
`prod_Ikb`, with `Ikk`, `NfkIkb`, `Ikb` and `nIkb` free; the guide keeps the totals as parameters
of `Pimpl()`.

```{r steadystate}
```

## Events and switches

TNFα is added at time 0: an event replaces `TNF` by `dose_TNF`, 1 under stimulation and 0 in the
control. Event times and values may be parameters; the sensitivities pass the event. A switch on a
state needs no event: `"piecewise(kon, A > A0, koff)"` switches the rate when `A` crosses `A0`,
with exact sensitivities ([cppDE > Events](https://dmodverse.github.io/cppDE/articles/methods-events.html)).

## Prediction functions

`odemodel()` generates C++ code for the right-hand side and the sensitivity equations; `Xs()` turns
it into the `prdfn` `x`, `Y()` builds the observables `g` and the error model `e`. `compile =
FALSE` defers compilation to one joint `compile()`.

```{r odemodel}
```

The default backend `"cppDE"` integrates by BDF with first- and, with `deriv2 = TRUE`,
second-order sensitivities; `backend = "Sundials"` uses CVODES, `"deSolve"` deSolve. A step is
accepted if the weighted RMS norm of the local errors is at most one,
$\bigl(\tfrac1n \sum_i \varepsilon_i^2 / (\mathrm{atol} + \mathrm{rtol}\,|x_i|)^2\bigr)^{1/2} \le 1$:

| option | default | controls |
|---|---|---|
| `atol`, `rtol` | `1e-6`, `1e-6` | absolute and relative error per step |
| `maxsteps` | `1e6` | steps per solve |
| `maxattempts` | `50` | rejected steps in a row |
| `hini` | `0` | first step, 0 estimates it |
| `sensErrCon` | `TRUE` | (`optionsSens` only) sensitivities in the error test |

Logarithmic observables magnify the relative error of small states; `model.R` sets
`rtol = 1e-8`, `atol = 1e-10`.

`model.R` reads the CSV of the publication and keeps HepG2 cells without compound: 312 points in
two conditions.

```{r}
table(hepg2$name, hepg2$condition)
covariates(data)
```

`as.datalist()` splits the data by condition; `covariates()` lists the columns that describe the
conditions.

```{r, fig.height = 5}
plotData(data, name %in% c("nucNFkB", "cytNFkB", "A20GFP", "IkBa", "pIkBa", "pIKK")) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "time [min]", y = "log signal [a.u.]")
```

## Parameter transformation

`define()` and `insert()` build the assignments of the `parfn` `p`:

- `define("x <- x", x = ...)` takes every parameter of `pSS`, `x`, `g` and `e` except the states,
  whose values come from the steady state;
- `insert("x <- exp(x)", x = ...)` puts every symbol on the log scale;
- `define("TNF <- 0")` sets TNFα to 0 for the steady state;
- `branch(covariates(data))` copies the assignments per condition, `define(..., conditionMatch =)`
  sets the dose.

```{r transformation}
```

```{r}
getEquations(p, conditions = "TNF")[c("dose_TNF", "TNF", "totalNfk", "Vnuc")]
getEquations(p, conditions = "control")[c("dose_TNF", "TNF")]
```

`compile()` builds all sources into one shared object in `getOption("dMod2.outdir")` and reuses
object files whose source and flags are unchanged.

```{r compile}
```

```{r}
length(getParameters(prd))
```

## Likelihood and prior

`normL2(data, prd, e)` returns $-2 \log L$ with gradient and Gauss-Newton Hessian
([Methods > Likelihood and prior](methods-objective.html)). `constraintL2()` adds a Gaussian prior
on the log scale, which keeps parameters the data do not determine finite; the multistart of
[Optimization](guide-optimization.html) draws the starts from it. Mean 0 and standard deviation 4,
a factor of $e^4 \approx 55$, for parameters of unknown magnitude; narrower where the magnitude is
known:

| parameters | mean | sd | reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| bleaching rates `tau_*` | $\log(0.1/360)$ | 2 | about 10 % of signal lost over six hours |
| imaging noise `sigma_*` | $\log 0.05$ | 1 | replicates scatter by about 5 % |
| basal rates `*_Base` | $-8$ | 2 | activation without TNFα far slower than with it |
| `shuttle_RnaA20`, `degrad_RnaA20`, `build_A20`, `degrad_A20`, `degrad_mIkb` | $\log(1/60)$ | 2 | transcripts and A20 turn over within about an hour |
| `trigger_iIkk` | $\log(1/240)$ | 2 | IKK recovers over hours |

Starts far outside these ranges end on plateaus where a signal bleaches away, the noise explains
every residual or A20 follows NFκB within minutes.

`pSS` returns unstable roots too (`controlsPTC = list(stability = FALSE)`);
`constraintStability()` adds a term that is zero on a stable resting state, rises on a ramp below
the stability boundary, a tenth of the inverse time span of the data wide (`width`, about 2.8e-4
per minute), and reaches 100 for each eigenvalue at the boundary. It needs
`Pimpl(deriv2 = TRUE)`. Profiles with `stop = "data"` and likelihood ratios read the data term
without it ([Methods > Steady states](methods-steady-states.html#stability)).

```{r objective}
```

```{r tolerances}
```

## Model evaluation

```{r, echo = FALSE}
invisible(stored("results/fits.rds", "fit.R"))
```

At the best fit of [Optimization](guide-optimization.html), with the parameters fixed by the gauge
of [Symmetries](guide-symmetries.html):

```{r gauge, echo = FALSE}
```

```{r}
best <- as.parvec(readRDS("results/fits.rds"))
value <- obj(best, fixed = gauge)
c(value = value$value, data = attr(value, "data"), prior = attr(value, "prior"))
max(abs(value$gradient))
```

The prediction against the data, with one standard deviation of the error model as a band,
each observable up to the last time point of the data:

```{r, fig.height = 7}
times <- seq(0, 360, length.out = 361)
last <- pmax(with(lbind(data), tapply(time, name, max)), 30)
plotCombined(prd(times, c(best, gauge), deriv = FALSE), data, time <= last[as.character(name)],
             errfn = e) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free", ncol = 4) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "time [min]", y = "log signal [a.u.]")
```
